title.narrative: Creation of 4 decentralized mining administration offices (BAM)

comment.narrative: Although the process of establishing BAMs was adequately launched, only 2 out of 4 targeted were created and none actuallyfunctions as intended at the time of closure. The BAMs pilots lost of their relevance especially after the 2008 ban of rough stonesexports.The most significant pilot took place in Vatomandry where around 6-7000 miners rushed on rubies from 2001. After apromising start of the BAM which helped train around 500 artisans.

title.narrative: Mining Environmental Management Units established in all Provinces

comment.narrative: PGRM established and supported one central and six decentralized environment Units in main mining regions. Those Units havesuccessfully been integrated within the Ministry of Mines’ organization and staff hired as civil servants, ensuring sustainability.

title.narrative: Number of community development plans that include management of mineral resources

comment.narrative: End result could reach 15 if inter-communal plans are counted and 18 if Ambatovy communes are counted.

PGRM supported communities in many communes in integrating mineral resources and revenues into their local development plan andbudgets. On artisanal mining, pilots on gold management were developed in 9 communes. On industrial mining, the participatorybudgetingprocess focused on 3 communes in Fort Dauphin and was extended to 3 others around the Ambatovy project (in partnershipwith another World Bank Project). In addition, 3 inter-communal development plans were developed to integrate mining development.

comment.narrative: Gemstones exchanges were also organized in regions but most of the trading has gradually concentrated in the capital.

title.narrative: Increase in reported exports of gold and gemstones

comment.narrative: A reliable statistical and export data system was being developed with the support of PGRM. Not completed and finalization will bedelayed

title.narrative: Number of small artisans trained and certified in gem processing techniques

target.value: At least 20 individualscertified each year of pro

comment.narrative: IGM has successfully trained many Malagasy artisans or entrepreneurs thanks to PGRM continued support. 1,750 individuals weretrained (195 per year) and around 95% of them obtaining there certificates.

Although the process of establishing BAMs was adequately launched, only 2 out of 4 targeted were created and none actuallyfunctions as intended at the time of closure. The BAMs pilots lost of their relevance especially after the 2008 ban of rough stonesexports.The most significant pilot took place in Vatomandry where around 6-7000 miners rushed on rubies from 2001. After apromising start of the BAM which helped train around 500 artisans in 2004-2005, the dynamic of the rush reversed in 2006, thereserves were exhaustedand the mining sites around that location were gradually abandoned.

title.narrative: Declared exports of gold and gemstones

comment.narrative: Available statistics show that official exports for gold plus gemstones were around 30 million dollars in 2008, after a peak ofaround 40 million in 2006.

title.narrative: Studies on decentralized management of mineral resources

comment.narrative: Several studies were completed. One major piece on Anosy was achieved in 2006, and 3 inter-communal schemes to integrate miningdevelopment into local and regional development were conducted in 2012.

title.narrative: Backlog of overdue application of mining permits

comment.narrative: Not exceeding 5% of all permits

The Madagascar mining cadastre (BCMM) was a model in Africa until the political crisis, and mining permits were efficientlyallocated (although data on time average still need to be completed). However, since the political crisis a de facto moratorium onpermit allocations has been imposed. In April 2012 almost 3000 requests were pending. This number is expected to be reduced withPGRM supportby end of June.

title.narrative: Increase in the collection rate of mining royalty as a result of decentralized tax collection procedures

comment.narrative: The Ministry of Mines have statistics on expected and collected royalties based on number of "laissez passer" (for artisanalmining) and projected production (industrial mining). They show an increase of collection rate throughout the project period thanksto measures like the one-stop shop, but also the effect of industrial mining coming on stream. Figures do not include informalproduction,for which there is no statistics.

The Ministry of Mines have statistics on expected and collected royalties based on number of "laissez passer" for artisanalmining.Figures of 2008 (as targeted in the PAD) show 60% against 80% in 2006 and 100% in 2010.

title.narrative: Sector Environmental and Social Assessment (SESA) completed by mid term review

comment.narrative: SESA was realized by end of 2003.

title.narrative: One-stop shop for export of gemstones

comment.narrative: The One-stop shop for gemstones export was established by the Arrete n°12506/2003. Conceived and equipped by the project, itstillcentralizes in one location all sectoral and customs formalities for gemstones export.

title.narrative: Creation of one-stop shop for exports of gemstones

comment.narrative: The one-stop shop is in place and jointly run by Mining and Customs administration staff.After a period of anarchical rushes onsapphire and ruby, such measures helped reducing long paper export procedures, limited one incentive to smuggle, and effectivelycontributed to an increase of formal exports.

title.narrative: Set up of certificate of origins

comment.narrative: The project supported certification of gemstones mainly through the creation of IGM. No specific certificate of "Malagasy stones"have been undertaken (and actually planned) by the project. PGRM had however an critical role in certifying exports, and buildingthereputation of Madagascar in the international gemstones market before the 2008 ban.

title.narrative: Territorial conservation practises in ASM areas improved and Resitution of previous conditions after exploration

comment.narrative: This indicator had no specific definition. PGRM undertook sensitization campaigns in ASM settlements on environment management. Italso developed tools for better controlling artisanal mining rushes. More information is needed to document that aspect in projectpilot areas.

Last figure available is the 2009 2.9 billion investment (Central Bank) due mainly to Ambatovy. This does not reflect a trend butclearly demonstrates the scope of mining development in the country. Annual investment has also grown due to explorationexpenditures.

title.narrative: Increase of mining fiscal revenues for provinces and communes

comment.narrative: In pilot communes, increase of fiscal revenues due to mining is clear. Sample data are expected by end of project.

A comprehensive assessment of the mining fiscal framework was conducted and recommendations submitted early 2009. The politicalcrisis has prevented follow up reforms at this point, but the Government has background, legal and fiscal analysis needed toenvisage changes in the future.

title.narrative: Mechanisms to ensure a fair participation and usage of mining fiscal revenues

comment.narrative: A series of studies and workshop took place in the Anosy region to devise possible mechanisms for channeling mining royalties atthe regional and local level in a more sustainable way. The consensus reached end of 2008 focused on the creation of a MiningCommunity Foundation. All the preparatory work (feasibility works, consultations, status) were prepared. The draft Decree wasproposed just before the political crisis which interrupted the discussion.

title.narrative: National Geological Survey and the integrated sector data bank and information systems have been established

comment.narrative: PGRM has created the BPGRM, the center for geoscientific data which is the core of a National Geological Survey. A study on itssustainability and its possible externalization out of the Direction of Geology where it has successfully been integrated wasundertaken in the last year of the project. Given the political context, it is unlikely that the institutional reform needed totake that final step happen before closure.

PGRM has supported the creation of the Environment cells which combined with the decentralized offices of the Cadastre and theDirection of Mines were supposed to be integrated in the new Mining Inspectorate. The key pieces are therefore in place, but giventhe political context, it is unlikely that the institutional reform needed to take the final step of its creation as an agencyhappens before closure.

title.narrative: Inter-ministerial coordination and adjustments to the legal and institutional frameworks

comment.narrative: PGRM supported different coordination mechanisms, most importantly the CGIM, a special inter-ministerial commission in charge ofthe monitoring of LGIM contracts. PGRM facilitated its creation and funded its permanent technical secretariat. CGIM has been themainarm of the Government to negotiate with candidate large-scale mining companies and oversee their investments, in particular theAmbatovy one. The Commission is still operational and the Secretariat will be integrated within the Ministry of Mines after projectclosure.

title.narrative: Methodologies to facilitate and promote the integration of large scale mining projects into local economic development

comment.narrative: PGRM supported participatory budgeting at municipal level and provided much technical assistance to the two main mining regions tobetter integrate industrial mining at the decentralized levels.

title.narrative: Financial mechanisms for long term sustainability of mining institutions

comment.narrative: Sustainability studies started early 2009 but had to be stopped when the crisis hit. They successfully resumed in the last year ofthe project and produced recommendations for the short and medium term.

title.narrative: Methodologies to control ASM rushes and to manage conflicts between ASM activities and protected areas

comment.narrative: The project supported the production of a toolkit for management of ASM in or around protected areas.

title.narrative: Plan with specific time based measures for the restructuring of OMNIS adopted

comment.narrative: This indicator does not refer to PGRM- funded activities. It was included in the AF because it was part of a coordinationagreementwith Norway which was launching a project on hydrocarbon aspects in parallel (see the coordination matrix in the ProjectPaper Annex). The Oil for Development Project of Norway was active until February 2009, but was canceled following the politicalcrisis. The work on OMNIS restructuring had only been initiated in 2008.

title.narrative: Training of staff at the agencies in charge of hydrocarbons and mining implemented;

comment.narrative: Training on petroleum was the responsibility of Norway cooperation (as part of a coordination mechanism, see explanation in otherpetroleum-related indicators). PGRM did finance much training on mining for many staff of different institutions, including thePIU, the BPGRM, the Environment Cells, the CGIM, the BCMM, the Direction of Mines, the Direction of Geology.

title.narrative: Education and training programs related to Extractive Industries at Madagascar universities

comment.narrative: PGRM financed much training on mining for many staff of different institutions, including the PIU, the BPGRM, the EnvironmentCells, the CGIM, the BCMM, the Direction of Mines, the Direction of Geology. A few PhD at university were supported as part of theknowledge transfer in geology contracts.

title.narrative: Percentage of value added to gemstones in the country

comment.narrative: This indicator does not have a clear definition and target. Value addition in the gemstones market was ensured mainly through thecreation of IGM and subsequent business development in cutting and polishing. There are presently numerous lapidaries and jeweleryinthe capital. Estimates are expected by end of project.
